solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Actor drawing on toilet wall?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the drawing comes after the toilet

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, the wall where the drawing sits
a drawing is a piece of art

explanation.surface: Someone asks which film star scribbled graffiti in the gents.
explanation.walkthrough: BOG is everyday British slang for a lavatory, so 'bog art' is toilet graffiti; the question mark flags the pun on the film star's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a famous Hollywood film star, so the surname stands for an actor.

clue.text: Courage perhaps shown by British Navy at last capturing vessel

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the vessel goes within
at last means the final letter of navy

parts.note: a ewer is a jug, a vessel

explanation.surface: Bravery displayed by the British navy as it seizes a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Courage is a British beer brand, so its maker is an example of a brewery; 'perhaps' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage was a well-known British beer company, so it is an example of a brewing business.

clue.text: Start publishing work about saints received in advance

indicators.note: in advance puts the received piece first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: got means received
op is short for opus, a work
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Beginning a print run of a book on saints paid for upfront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like part of the publishing picture, but 'in advance' just puts the received piece at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to press is to begin printing a newspaper or book, so publishing starts.

clue.text: Take back abusive comments about European Commission's leader

indicators.note: about means around, so the rant goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rant is a stream of angry abusive words

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Commission

explanation.surface: Withdrawing insulting remarks about the head of the European Commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RANT around E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement formally, which is to take it back.

clue.text: Concentrated in class, not very bright to start with

indicators.note: says the dim piece comes first, ahead of the class

parts.note: a dim person is called thick
a set is a class or group at school

explanation.surface: A student is said to have focused in lessons despite being slow at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrated' reads as a studious verb, but it is the adjective: plants set densely together are thickset.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset can mean set or growing closely together, densely packed, as a thickset hedge is.

clue.text: Timid creature abducts maiden from group of girls

indicators.note: abducts means carries away, so the maiden is taken out

parts.note: a harem is a group of women
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A shy animal kidnaps a young woman from a group.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring M stands for a maiden over.
explanation.definitionFit: The hare is a timid animal that bolts at danger, so it is a timid creature.

clue.text: Earnest campaigner flogged used car, right?

indicators.note: flogged means beaten, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Asking whether a second-hand car was sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' is British slang for sold, but here it rearranges USED CAR into CRUSADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Was Dizzy Gillespie's second teacher

parts.note: a dizzy person's head swam
the second letter of Gillespie is I

explanation.surface: Asking whether jazz trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie had a second music teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Dizzy Gillespie was a jazz trumpeter, but 'Was Dizzy' gives SWAM, as in one's head swam.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, so the word stands for a teacher.

clue.text: Visibly upset by t-telling off

parts.note: the stammered t- gives the letter T
an earful is a telling-off, a scolding

explanation.surface: Someone stammers, upset by a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer adds a T before EARFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful means crying or near tears, which is being visibly upset.

clue.text: Attract English tourists principally into resort

indicators.note: says the tourists' leading letter is put inside the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: principally means taking the first, principal letter of tourists

explanation.surface: A travel slogan about luring British holidaymakers to a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts T inside NICE to make NTICE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone, a close synonym of attract.

clue.text: Noise of merriment after drink's said to create fuss

indicators.note: says the laughter comes after the drink in the answer
said tells us we want only the sound of the word for drink, not its spelling

parts.note: brew is a word for a drink such as beer or tea; the 's is a link
ha-ha is the sound of laughter

explanation.surface: Laughter following a round of drinks is said to cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a drink is said aloud, so its sound is wanted, not its spelling; 'to create' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or uproar, which is what a fuss is.

clue.text: Messenger, drunk, hugs copper

indicators.note: hugs means holds around, so the copper goes inside

parts.note: merry means tipsy, a bit drunk
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A tipsy courier embraces a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal. Mercury was messenger of the Roman gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was the messenger of the gods in Roman myth.

clue.text: Former leaders of political system seen fiddling what they claim?

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so these letters are rearranged
leaders of means taking the first letters of political and system

explanation.surface: Ex-politicians are seen fiddling, a dig at the parliamentary expenses scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges P, S and SEEN into PENSES. The surface recalls the 2009 British MPs' expenses scandal, where members fiddled their claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Expenses are the costs that politicians claim back, so they are what such people claim.

clue.text: Row about gas charges

definitions.note: a tariff is a list or scale of charges, so the plural fits

indicators.note: about says the quarrel goes around the gas

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel or row
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas

explanation.surface: An argument over gas bills.
explanation.walkthrough: Row here means a quarrel, not a line, and the gas is argon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a fixed schedule of prices or duties, the charges made for something.

clue.text: Fault lines enthral old governor

parts.note: a vice is a moral fault

indicators.note: enthral means hold captive, so the lines hold the old

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines

explanation.surface: Moral weakness grips a former colonial ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fault lines' looks like geology, but it splits into two pieces; 'enthral' puts the old inside the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A viceroy ruled a colony on a monarch's behalf, as in British India.

clue.text: Frenchman is against entering into agreement

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the word of agreement

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
v is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is opposed to joining a pact.
explanation.walkthrough: V for versus goes into YES; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French man's name, as in Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Crash with a student in flat?

parts.note: a crash is a road accident
L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A car crash involving a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: In music an accidental is a sign such as a flat or sharp; the question mark shows a flat is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat sign in music is one kind of accidental, alongside sharps and naturals.

clue.text: Soundly instructed in science as new innovation, perhaps

indicators.note: soundly says only the spoken form of the word for instructed is wanted

parts.note: taught means instructed
an ology is a branch of science

explanation.surface: Being well taught in science counts as a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new innovation' says the same thing twice, an example of needless repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tautology says the same thing twice, and new innovation does exactly that.

clue.text: Banks are collapsing in location of Lincoln

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Banks are going bust in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the English city, but it is the capital of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is the state capital of Nebraska in the United States.

clue.text: Take away bottle as the diner ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer has a wine bottle removed after ordering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, so taking away someone's bottle is to dishearten them; 'ordered' looks like a diner's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to make someone lose courage, and bottle is British slang for nerve.

clue.text: Raising hat to woman could present a problem

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the hat is turned around

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Tipping one's hat to a lady could cause difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns LID upwards to give DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, so it is a problem.

clue.text: Son appears in competition to make a point

indicators.note: appears in says the son is placed inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, as in the FA Cup

explanation.surface: A boy enters a contest to prove something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; 'a point' is the definition, not a debating aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end where two curves meet, such as the point of a crescent moon.

clue.text: Soup that's of little value when you make a mess of it

definitions.meaning: a thick vegetable soup or stew

definitions.text: that's of little value when you make a mess of it
definitions.meaning: a mess of the stew is the phrase for something of trifling worth, from Esau selling his birthright

explanation.walkthrough: Esau sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, called a mess of pottage, the phrase for a worthless trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is a thick soup, and a mess of it means something of little worth.

clue.text: A measure of material for Peter?

definitions.meaning: a unit of the fineness of yarn, used for stockings
the apostle who three times disowned Jesus, one who says no

explanation.walkthrough: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times, so he is one who denies.
explanation.definitionFit: Denier is a unit of yarn fineness, and also one who denies something.

clue.text: Expert's left for week with this creature

indicators.note: left for week says one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a wizard is an expert; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A specialist leaves for a week, taking a reptile along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert's' is Expert is: change W for L in WIZARD and you get this creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard is a scaly reptile, so it is the creature the clue points to.

clue.text: Spanish hero's final letter to bespectacled bishop?

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
RR, Right Reverend, a bishop, inside OO, a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: A Spanish hero's last letter goes to a bishop in glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) sits between two Os that look like a pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorro is the masked Spanish swordsman hero of fiction and film.

clue.text: Leading doctor's tense after warning

indicators.note: says the doctor and tense come after the warning

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; MO's gives MOS
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A medic is nervous after being cautioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore!' is the cry golfers shout to warn people of a ball in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank or position, which is leading.

clue.text: What baby does, making delivery heard

indicators.note: heard means we want how the word for delivery sounds

parts.note: a ball is a delivery from a bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: A baby is born crying loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth, but in cricket a bowler's delivery is a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies cry loudly, and to bawl is to cry noisily.

clue.text: What footballer does? He shoots

definitions.meaning: a defender marks, or shadows, an opposing man
a sharpshooter, someone skilled with a gun

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, MARKS MAN is what a defender does to an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a skilled shooter, and a footballer marks a man in defence.

clue.text: Plant elements of Maoism all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bits of Maoist thought turn up everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub or tree, the sensitive plant among them.

clue.text: Lovely beer to take on board at sea

indicators.note: to take on means to hold or carry, so the beer goes around the other letters

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beer is stowed on a ship at sea, which sounds delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges BOARD into DORAB, which ALE takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming and delightful, so it is a synonym of lovely.

clue.text: Seaside feature contributing to return of teeny organisms

indicators.note: return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beach structure helps tiny creatures come back.
explanation.walkthrough: ENYORG is hidden in 'teeny organisms', and 'return of' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to stop beach erosion.
